result.topic_en: The page finishes worked examples of finding numbers via $qq = 10z^2+1$ with $y=2z$, giving sums of squares of the form $(\dots+1)^2+(\dots+1)^2=\square$, and then begins fragment 50, a 'most difficult problem': finding four fourth powers whose sum is a fourth power, $A^4+B^4+C^4+D^4=E^4$.
result.transcription:
216 L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA. Arithmetica.

$x=\frac{zz+yy+1}{2z}$, hinc $qq=\frac{yzz+y^3+y}{z}-1$.

Statuatur nunc $y=nz$ fietque $qq=nzz+n^3zz+n-1$. Capiatur ergo $n=2$, ut sit $y=2z$, erit $qq=10z^2+1$, cui satisfit:

1) Si $z=\frac{2}{3}$; tum erit $qq=\frac{49}{9}$, ergo $q=\frac{7}{3}$. Porro $y=\frac{4}{3}$, unde $x=\frac{29}{12}$ et $p=\frac{7}{4}$. Tum igitur formula $\left(\frac{49}{16}+1\right)^2+\left(\frac{49}{9}+1\right)^2$, erit quadratum radicis $xx+yy=\frac{841}{144}+\frac{16}{9}=\frac{1097}{144}$.

2) Sumatur $z=\frac{2}{9}$, erit $qq=\frac{121}{81}$, hinc $q=\frac{11}{9}$; tum vero $y=\frac{4}{9}$ et $x=\frac{5zz+1}{2z}=\frac{101}{36}$, ergo
$p=\frac{101}{81}-\frac{2}{9}=\frac{83}{81}$.

3) Sumatur $z=6$, erit $qq=361$ et $q=19$, porro $y=12$ et $x=\frac{181}{12}$ et $p=\frac{109}{12}$, ergo
$\left(\frac{109^2}{144}+1\right)^2+(361+1)^2=\left(\frac{181^2}{144}+144\right)^2$.

A. m. T. I. p. 279.

50.

Problema difficillimum,

quo quatuor biquadrata quaeruntur, quorum summa itidem sit biquadratum,
sive ut sit $A^4+B^4+C^4+D^4=E^4$,
siquidem fieri potest, sequenti modo tractandum videtur:

Statuatur scilicet $A^2=\frac{pp+qq+rr-ss}{n}$, $B^2=\frac{2ps}{n}$, $C^2=\frac{2qs}{n}$ et $D^2=\frac{2rs}{n}$; tum enim fiet
$E^2=\frac{pp+qq+rr+ss}{n}$,
ita, ut haec quinque formulae quadrata reddi debeant. Incipiamus a prima et ultima, ita, ut reddi debeat
$\frac{pp+qq+rr}{n}\pm\frac{ss}{n}=\square$.
Cum igitur sit $aa+bb\pm2ab=\square$, statuatur
$\frac{pp+qq+rr}{n}=aa+bb$ et $\frac{ss}{n}=2ab$,
fit ergo $ss=2nab=\square$. Sit $2n=\alpha\beta$ et statuatur $a=\alpha ff$ et $b=\beta gg$ eritque
$ss=\alpha\alpha\beta\beta ffgg$, ergo $s=\alpha\beta fg=2nfg$;
tum vero esse debet $\frac{pp+qq+rr}{n}=\alpha\alpha f^4+\beta\beta g^4$.
Pro reliquis conditionibus faciamus $\frac{2ps}{n}=4pfg=4xx$, unde $p=\frac{xx}{fg}$, porro $\frac{2qs}{n}=4qfg=4yy$, hinc $q=\frac{yy}{fg}$, pro quarta $\frac{2rs}{n}=4rfg=4zz$, habemus $r=\frac{zz}{fg}$. Hinc superest ista aequatio
$\frac{pp+qq+rr}{n}=\alpha\alpha f^4+\beta\beta g^4$, sive $pp+qq+rr=\frac{1}{2}\alpha\beta(\alpha\alpha f^4+\beta\beta g^4)$,
et loco $p$, $q$, $r$ valores inventos substituendo
$\frac{x^4}{f^2g^2}+\frac{y^4}{f^2g^2}+\frac{z^4}{f^2g^2}=\frac{1}{2}\alpha\beta(\alpha\alpha f^4+\beta\beta g^4)$, sive $x^4+y^4+z^4=\frac{1}{2}\alpha\beta ffgg(\alpha\alpha f^4+\beta\beta g^4)$.

methods.what: Substitution $y=nz$ reducing the condition to $qq=nzz+n^3zz+n-1$; with $n=2$ this becomes $qq=10z^2+1$

methods.what: Numerical solutions of $qq=10z^2+1$ ($z=2/3, 2/9, 6$) giving explicit identities of the form $(\dots+1)^2+(\dots+1)^2=\square$
Parametrization making $A^4+B^4+C^4+D^4=E^4$ follow from five squares conditions

methods.what: Using $aa+bb\pm2ab=\square$ to satisfy the first and last square conditions, with $2n=\alpha\beta$, $a=\alpha ff$, $b=\beta gg$, giving $s=2nfg$
Reduction of the problem to the equation $x^4+y^4+z^4=\frac12\alpha\beta ffgg(\alpha\alpha f^4+\beta\beta g^4)$ via $p=xx/fg$, $q=yy/fg$, $r=zz/fg$
